metadata.title: Pass 3 reference table: prolate-spheroid blastoderm geometry, strain-rate-dependent Myosin-II recruitment, and cell-intercalation (T1 / rosette) topology for Drosophila germband extension
metadata.note: Values marked verified_offline=false were entered from the assessor's recollection of the cited papers and could not be checked against the DOI landing pages during the offline Pass 3 loop; treat them as approximate anchors, not digitised data. Values under *_parameters are modelling choices of 2018-streichan-global-morphogenetic-flow.py, not measurements.

sources.citation: Lefebvre MF, Claussen NH, Mitchell NP, Gustafson HJ, Streichan SJ (2023). Geometric control of myosin II orientation during axis elongation. eLife 12:e78787.
Brauns F, Claussen NH, Lefebvre MF, Wieschaus EF, Shraiman BI (2024). The geometric basis of epithelial convergent extension. eLife 13:RP95521.
Bertet C, Sulak L, Lecuit T (2004). Myosin-dependent junction remodelling controls planar cell intercalation and axis elongation. Nature 429(6992):667-671.
Blankenship JT, Backovic ST, Sanny JSP, Weitz O, Zallen JA (2006). Multicellular rosette formation links planar cell polarity to tissue morphogenesis. Developmental Cell 11(4):459-470.

prolate_spheroid_surface_geometry.embedding: X(s, phi) = (a cos s, b sin s cos phi, b sin s sin phi), s in (0, pi) polar angle from the anterior pole, phi azimuth with phi = 0 on the ventral midline
prolate_spheroid_surface_geometry.metric: g_ss = a^2 sin^2 s + b^2 cos^2 s,  g_phiphi = b^2 sin^2 s,  g_sphi = 0,  dA = sqrt(g_ss g_phiphi) ds dphi
prolate_spheroid_surface_geometry.gaussian_curvature: K(s) = a^2 / g_ss(s)^2;  K_equator = 1/a^2 = 1.60e-5 um^-2,  K_pole = a^2/b^4 = 5.14e-4 um^-2,  K_pole/K_equator = (a/b)^4 = 32.14
prolate_spheroid_surface_geometry.cartographic_lift: the Pass 2 flat patterns are sampled on the surface with x = a(1 - cos s) (axial coordinate, 0..500 um) and y = b sin s * phi (geodesic DV arc from the ventral midline, wrapped into the flat model's periodic [-210, 210] um)
prolate_spheroid_surface_geometry.note: The Pass 2 cartographic domain used L_DV = 420 um as 'circumference'; the geometric circumference of a 210 um wide circular cross-section is 2*pi*105 = 659.7 um. The Pass 3 curved solver uses the geometric metric and excludes 20 um radius pole caps (v = 0 there).

surface_stokes_brinkman.operator: -eta*Delta_B v^a - eta_b*nabla^a(nabla_b v^b) - eta*K*v^a + xi*v^a = nabla_b sigma_a^{ab}   (Bochner Laplacian Delta_B, Gaussian curvature K from the Ricci identity nabla_b nabla^a v^b = nabla^a nabla_b v^b + K v^a)
surface_stokes_brinkman.dissipation_functional: J[v] = int dA [ eta e_ab e^ab + 1/2 (eta_b - eta) (e^a_a)^2 + 1/2 xi g_ab v^a v^b + sigma_a^{ab} e_ab ],  e_ab = 1/2 (e_a . d_b v + e_b . d_a v) with the embedded tangent basis e_a = d_a X (exact covariant strain of a tangent field; no Christoffel symbols needed)
surface_stokes_brinkman.kernel_without_friction: Killing fields of the prolate spheroid: rigid rotation v^phi = const (zero viscous dissipation); friction xi > 0 removes it
surface_stokes_brinkman.analytic_check_on_sphere: for v = grad(psi) with Delta psi = -l(l+1)/R^2 psi the operator acts as the scalar (eta + eta_b) l(l+1)/R^2 - 2*eta/R^2 + xi (Weitzenboeck identity Delta_B grad psi = grad Delta psi + K grad psi); Lean Theorem 4 surface_stokes_brinkman_gradient_mode_pos proves this eigenvalue is >= xi > 0 for l >= 1

sphere_check_parameters.note: pointwise relative L2 residual of the discrete operator on interior nodes; 2nd-order central differences => residual ~ h^2

solver_parameters.director: e_phi_hat (DV cables run along circles of latitude), Q_phiphi = +1/2, Q_ss = -1/2
solver_parameters.velocity_calibration: single scale factor fixing the WT peak |V_s| at m = m_0 to 6.40 um/min (Streichan et al. 2018 Figs. 2-3)

strain_rate_dependent_myosin_recruitment.model: m_{n+1}(x) = m_0(x) * (1 + beta_fb * max(0, -e_nn[m_n](x)) / e_ref),  e_nn = strain rate along the junctional director (e_phiphi for DV cables; negative = contraction), iterated to the fixed point
strain_rate_dependent_myosin_recruitment.fixed_point: linearised at one node: m* = m_0 / (1 - g) for loop gain g = beta_fb * |e_nn| / (e_ref) per unit m_0 < 1; g >= 1 has no bounded fixed point (run-away recruitment); Lean Theorem 5 myosin_feedback_fixed_point
strain_rate_dependent_myosin_recruitment.source: Lefebvre et al. (2023) eLife 12:e78787 (strain-rate / tension dependent recruitment and geometric control of the director); reduced linear-feedback form chosen here, coefficients are modelling assumptions

cell_intercalation_topology.t1_transition: DV-oriented (vertical) junction shared by an anterior and a posterior cell shrinks to zero length; the dorsal and ventral cells gain a new AP-oriented junction (Bertet et al. 2004 Fig. 1)
cell_intercalation_topology.rosette: k >= 2 consecutive DV-oriented junctions of a multicellular myosin cable (k + 1 trivalent vertices) collapse into a single vertex of order r = k + 3 cells (5-11 cells observed, Blankenship et al. 2006); resolution creates r - 3 = k new AP-oriented junctions joining r - 2 = k + 1 trivalent vertices (a tree), so the junction count is conserved (Lean Theorem 6 rosette_resolution_junction_balance)
cell_intercalation_topology.junction_shrink_time_source: Bertet et al. (2004) Nature 429:667-671 (time-lapse of vertical junction shrinkage; approximate)
cell_intercalation_topology.intercalation_share_source: Brauns et al. (2024) eLife 13:RP95521 tension-isogonal decomposition: cell rearrangement (T1/rosette) carries the majority of wild-type germband extension, cell-shape (isogonal) deformation the remainder; midpoint of the approximate range, not a digitised value

ledger_parameters.note: k_shrink = 0.42/min gives ln(1/0.15)/0.42 = 4.5 min for a saturated junction; the Hill switch (m_half = 0.7, n = 8) restricts shrinkage to Myosin-II-enriched junctions so that the median shrink time falls inside the 5-10 min Bertet et al. (2004) window and the intercalation share inside the Brauns et al. (2024) 0.5-0.8 range; these two targets were used to pick (k_shrink, m_half, n) and are therefore calibrated, not predicted
